summary: AI observability has become one of the most consequential infrastructure decisions for LLM teams, with roughly 73% of enterprises now requiring AI agent monitoring in production. These tools provide tracing, cost tracking, quality metrics, and guardrails that separate production-grade teams from those flying blind. Choosing the right platform depends heavily on your workload type (RAG, agents, chatbots) and whether cost control or deep debugging is your priority.

tools.name: LangSmith
tools.monitors: Multi-step agent traces, unified workflow costs, latency, prompt/response quality, and evaluation runs across complex LLM pipelines.
features: Deep multi-step agent diagnostics and tracing
SmithDB backend with ~12x faster trace queries
tools.pricing: Free Developer tier (~5K traces/mo); Plus plan at $39 per seat/month; usage-based and enterprise tiers above.
tools.best_for: Teams building complex multi-step agents who need rich debugging, especially those already in the LangChain ecosystem.

tools.name: Helicone
tools.monitors: API requests, token usage, proxy-level costs, latency, caching efficiency, and per-model spend.
features: Consistent daily regression testing alongside production traffic
tools.pricing: Free tier (10,000 requests/mo); usage-based pricing above the free tier.
tools.best_for: Chatbots and cost-conscious teams wanting fast, low-friction setup via a gateway layer.

tools.name: Weights & Biases (W&B)
tools.monitors: LLM experiments, model training runs, prompts, traces, evaluations, and end-to-end ML+LLM lifecycle metrics.
features: Weave for LLM tracing and evaluation
Strong integration with traditional ML workflows
tools.pricing: Free tier for personal/academic use; team and enterprise plans priced per seat/usage (custom quotes for enterprise).
tools.best_for: Teams running both traditional ML and LLM workloads who want a single experiment-tracking and observability platform.

tools.name: Arize AI
tools.monitors: Production model and LLM performance, drift, embeddings, retrieval quality, and anomaly detection at scale.
features: Arize Phoenix for open-source LLM/RAG tracing
Retrieval quality and RAG evaluation metrics
tools.pricing: Phoenix is free/open-source; Arize AX offers a free tier with paid Pro and enterprise plans (custom pricing).
tools.best_for: RAG applications and production ML teams needing deep retrieval-quality metrics and drift detection.

tools.name: LangFuse
tools.monitors: Per-LLM-call costs, traces, sessions, user feedback, prompt versions, and multi-step agent debugging.
features: Multi-step agent debugging and session views
tools.pricing: Free open-source self-hosted option; managed cloud has a free Hobby tier with paid Core/Pro and enterprise plans.
tools.best_for: Agent and production teams wanting an open-source, self-hostable observability stack with granular cost tracking.

tools.name: OpenLLMetry
tools.monitors: LLM calls, token usage, latency, and traces via OpenTelemetry-standard instrumentation, exportable to any OTel backend.
features: Auto-instrumentation for popular LLM SDKs and vector DBs
Exports to Datadog, Grafana, Honeycomb, and other OTel backends
tools.pricing: Free and open-source (SDK); costs depend on the chosen OTel backend. Managed Traceloop platform offers free and paid tiers.
tools.best_for: Teams wanting standards-based, vendor-neutral instrumentation that plugs into existing observability infrastructure.

cost_tips: Use a gateway/proxy layer (e.g., Helicone or Portkey) with response caching to avoid paying for repeated or identical prompts.
Route requests intelligently: use smaller, cheaper models for simple tasks and reserve frontier models only for complex reasoning.
Trim token usage by compressing prompts, limiting context window size, and setting sensible max_token output caps.
Monitor per-call and per-feature spend continuously so you can catch cost spikes, runaway agents, and inefficient prompts early.
